items.heading: There Is No Universal Winner
items.text: There is no universal winner here, and anyone who tells you there is has not looked closely at both the exam data and the salary data at the same time.

items.heading: Most People Compare These Two
items.text: Most people compare these two fields using job titles and salary numbers before they have ever looked at what an actual Tuesday afternoon looks like in each one. That is backwards.

items.heading: This Is Where the Two
items.text: This is where the two fields diverge the most structurally, and where most people underestimate how different the entry cost really is.

rows: Build models, judge whether a deal, stock, budget, or investment makes sense, and argue for a decision using numbers as evidence.

A filing deadline collides with incomplete client data, or an audit finds a discrepancy nobody can explain yet.
Excel and financial modelling, Bloomberg/Refinitiv terminals, valuation frameworks (DCF, comparables), PowerPoint for pitch decks.

Senior bankers, portfolio managers, business heads, or founders, mostly forward-looking, "what should we do" conversations.

visuals.heading: Our Strongest Suggestion

figures.label: Education Budget
figures.source: Our strongest suggestion: keep a course or degree fee near a tenth of the family's total education budget, and treat spending above roughly a fifth as a serious caution. An illustration, not a real fee: on a Rs 8 lakh budget, a tenth is Rs 80,000, and the rest can fund exam fees, a laptop, one skill course and a reserve. A high-income skill portfolio built beside the credential is the base of an earlier path to financial freedom.
